Executive Summary

This report presents the findings of an automated GDPR compliance analysis covering 23 websites across multiple categories and regions. The analysis examines pre-consent tracking behavior, dark pattern usage in cookie consent banners, and the effectiveness of various privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) as countermeasures.

A large majority of sites (81.8%) were found to set tracking cookies before any user consent was given, violating GDPR Article 5(3). The average compliance score across all sites was 46.3 out of 100.

A large majority of sites (78.3%) employed at least one dark pattern in their cookie consent interface, undermining the principle of freely given consent.

Among the browser-based PETs evaluated, brave_shields proved most effective, reducing tracker exposure by an average of 95.1%.

Differential Privacy

Differential privacy mechanisms (Laplace, Gaussian, and Randomized Response) were applied to the aggregate compliance metrics to evaluate the feasibility of publishing statistics while protecting individual website data. Multiple privacy budgets (epsilon) were tested.

Recommended epsilon for publication: N/A

User Recommendations

  1. Install brave_shields for the strongest browser-level tracker blocking (avg. 95.1% reduction).
  2. firefox_etp_strict is a good alternative with 87.9% avg reduction.
  3. When a site uses Didomi, the reject/decline mechanism is most effective (PET score: 75.1).
  4. Be cautious with No CMP Detected-powered banners — they scored lowest as a privacy tool (PET score: 20.7).
  5. For maximum protection, combine brave_shields with a site using Didomi (est. 98.8% effective).
  6. Always click 'Reject All' when possible — some CMPs actually honour it.
  7. Differential privacy with moderate epsilon (≈1.0) can protect individual browsing data when publishing aggregate compliance statistics.

Methodology

This analysis was conducted using an automated pipeline built in Python. Websites were crawled using Playwright in three consent states: no interaction, accept all, and reject all. Cookies and HTTP requests were captured in each state.

Sites analyzed: 23  |  Categories: 8  |  Regions: 6

Pipeline Components

  1. Crawler — Playwright-based browser automation capturing cookies, HTTP requests, consent banners, and screenshots.
  2. Classifier — Cookie/tracker classification using EasyList, EasyPrivacy, Disconnect lists, and a fallback heuristic.
  3. Dark Pattern Detector — Detects 7 types of deceptive consent UI patterns.
  4. Compliance Scorer — GDPR compliance scoring (0–100) based on 6 weighted criteria.
  5. Metrics Engine — Aggregate statistics across all sites.
  6. PET Evaluator — Tests 7 browser-level PET configurations.
  7. DP Reporter — Applies differential privacy to aggregate metrics.
  8. CMP Analyzer — Evaluates consent management platforms as privacy tools.
  9. Visualizer — Generates 11 publication-quality figures (300 DPI).

Limitations

  • Consent banner interaction relies on keyword-based button detection; some non-standard banners may be missed.
  • Analysis is based on a single crawl per site; dynamic content may vary across visits.
  • Browser PET evaluation with extensions requires manual extension installation.
  • Results may vary depending on geographic location and VPN configuration.
